- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after sharp spikes.
- When sentiment is negative or neutral (≤0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly, especially if recent prices are falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after a price spike (e.g., +5–10% above true), especially if sentiment was positive just before; apply downward correction of 2–5% for such cases.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; check for lagged correction — apply upward bias only after sentiment confirms positive trend.
- Mean reversion is common in 30-day forecasts — if model is far above or below 18-day moving average, adjust toward it, especially if sentiment is mixed or neutral.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model tends to ignore sentiment volatility — if sentiment swings sharply, forecast should reflect recent sentiment direction, not just average.
